A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Mansformer to Concertormer with substantial revisions. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 includes readable supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original deblurring, deraining and SIDD denoising results, qualitative comparisons and component ablations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: V2 reports original restoration results, component and receptive-field analyses, a Restormer adaptation experiment, and supplementary denoising results and visual comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 adds Cross-Dimensional Communication projections and convolutions across attention maps before softmax (Section 4.1, Equations 8–9), extending v1's independently computed attention branches. It also revises block allocations and implements CSA within Restormer. The multi-scale U-Net, four spatial/channel branches and gdMLP remain recognizable.

E1.justification: Test1200 is removed from deraining evaluation. The other restoration tasks and principal datasets remain, including SIDD in v2's supplement. RealBlur testing was already stated in v1, so its newly supplied results do not establish newly added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds DeepRFT+, Uformer, MPRNet-local and DiffIR to the quantitative GoPro/HIDE comparison; Uformer already appeared in v1's figures. The newly reported RealBlur comparison includes BANet and FMIMO-UNet+ among its comparators. Qualitative comparisons also add DiffIR and, for deraining, DIDMDN.

E3.justification: The 600,000-iteration GoPro curriculum changes from 200k/300k/100k iterations at 128/256/384-pixel patches to 200k per stage at 128/256/320 pixels. AdamW beta2 changes from 0.999 to 0.9, and rotations are added. Ablations switch from 128- to 256-pixel patches, RealBlur uses fine-tuning rather than GoPro-only training, and new analyses introduce diffusion-index measurements and a Restormer comparison.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the component ablations and adds tests of the CSA prototype, concatenation, CDC and retaining versus omitting the global mean (Tables 5–6). Figure 8 examines receptive fields through local attribution maps, and Table 7 tests transfer to Restormer. V1's separate cross-attention, shifted-window and multi-head ablations are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's diffusion-index analysis does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: GoPro results change from 34.27/34.33 dB for Mansformer-E/P to 34.18/34.42 for Concertormer-lite/full. V2 adds RealBlur-R/J results of 40.78/33.51 dB, new analytical results and supplementary visual comparisons. REDS and deraining scores change; SIDD reports two configurations at 40.28/40.32 versus v1's single 40.32. Models and training differ, and deraining averages exclude Test1200, so these are not unchanged-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.1 introduces a formal shared-mean and residual decomposition and derives the prototype, tensorized CSA and CDC formulations. It adds assumptions concerning projected concatenation and absorbing or replacing the mean. V1 directly defines the four attention operations; its explicit per-branch and total complexity expressions are omitted in v2.

C1.justification: V2 makes CDC a separate central contribution and claims CSA can improve existing restoration backbones, including Restormer. It retains linear-complexity local/global modeling and single-stage gdMLP. V1's concluding claim of state-of-the-art denoising performance is removed, with denoising described as comparable in the supplement.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking shared attention and CDC to receptive-field expansion and discussing why concatenation and omission of the global mean help (Section 6.2). V1 attributes marginal SIDD gains to small images limiting useful global context and suggests convolutions may be preferable. V2 replaces that explanation with a limitation concerning careful backbone design for different restoration tasks.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies block size, head allocation and multi-scale spatial/frequency-domain L1 losses. Its supplement supplies SIDD and deraining training schedules, REDS configuration instructions and the alternative denoising model's block allocation. V1 refers to supplementary settings without including them in the supplied PDF. These disclosures do not establish that previously unspecified settings changed; code release remains a future promise.

R1.justification: The broad positioning against CNN/U-Net restoration and efficient Transformers remains. V2 adds Talking-heads Attention and local attribution maps to support CDC and analysis, plus references for newer comparators such as DiffIR, DeepRFT and BANet. Several background references disappear, including those supporting the removed SVM analogy.

P1.justification: The manuscript is extensively rewritten around Concertormer and Concertino/Ripieno terminology. V2 adds a separate self-attention background section and an Analysis and Discussion section, reorganizes applications, and moves denoising and limitations into the supplement. The changes substantially alter the narrative beyond renaming.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, transposes the main benchmark table, redraws the architecture and self-attention diagrams, and adds attention-map and attribution visualizations. Figure 1 becomes a single HIDE plot with a logarithmic FLOPs axis, dropping the deraining panel. Qualitative figures are reformatted into compact crop grids, and the supplement adds Figures 9–20.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens mechanism evidence and reproducibility through the targeted analyses in Tables 6–7 and Figure 8, reported RealBlur comparisons, and newly supplied task-specific training details. These gains outweigh reduced Test1200 coverage and the loss of explicit complexity formulas. A retained ranking claim becomes inaccurate: Table 1 places Concertormer-lite at 34.18 dB on GoPro, below FFTformer's 34.21, despite claiming the proposed models occupy the top two positions.
